Subject: Proforma commit adjustment request

Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our procurement team reviewed the proforma (attached) and asked whether we can reduce the 12-month reserved floor by 30% for the first two quarters of the term. The ask is driven by a near-term funding reforecast and concern about GPU spot-price spikes affecting our unit economics.

Specifics: can Redwood offer a temporary reduction to the committed GPU slab for Q1/Q2 with a price-indexed true-up tied to a GPU cost index (or capped pass-through)? We prefer an approach that doesn't require renegotiating the entire schedule but gives us some headroom if external costs remain elevated.

Attachments: Novus_proforma_v1.xlsx

Appreciate any quick guidance — procurement needs to know whether to proceed to legal.

Best,
Jane

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>

Subject: Fwd: Proforma commit adjustment request

Team — fwd from Novus. They want a 30% temporary reduction to the 12-month floor for the first two quarters, with some kind of GPU-cost indexation or capped pass-through. Procurement wants a clear 'yes/no' before routing to legal.

Options I see (quick):
- Tiered start: 70% committed for Q1/Q2, ramp to 100% thereafter; offer a 6% credit to compensate liquidity impact.
- Indexation: link per-GPU token price to a market index with a +/- band and a cap at +20% pass-through.
- Short-term credit: hold current floor but offer a cash credit if GPU-costs exceed a threshold.

Notes/questions: any approval needed for a >20% effective discount vs list? Finance, can you run a 12/24 month sensitivity (attached expected usage profile) and flag break-even on margins? Legal: if we add indexation clause we need a simple mechanic and auditability (who verifies the index).

Attaching the Novus sheet and a blank proforma template; will draft a one-pager for Jane after your inputs.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

Ben —

I had a quick call with Jane earlier. Their runway pressure is real but they still want predictability for model rollout. I prefer the tiered-start approach (70% then ramp) + a GPU-indexed true-up with a 20% cap. That limits our downside while giving them flexibility.

I've prepared a revised proforma (proforma_v2.xlsx) with two options: (A) Tiered ramp + 4% onboarding credit; (B) Maintain floor but add a capped pass-through. Option A is easier operationally.

Finance: can you flag the expected margin impact if we go with Option A and absorb the onboarding credit? If it's within the 8% tolerance we discussed, I'll propose Option A to Novus and request exec sign-off for the credit.

Karthik

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proforma commit adjustment request

Quick finance read: ran the sensitivity on the revised proforma. Highlights: 
- Option A (70% first two quarters, ramp to 100%): NPV impact over 12 months is ~-3.7% to gross margin, assuming current avg GPU costs.
- If GPU market increases by 25% sustained, margin hit could reach -9.8% over the year (worst-case).

Recommendation: approve Option A conditionally with two guardrails — (1) indexation true-up if GPU market > +15% (pass-through up to a 20% cap), (2) an exec-level approval clause for any concession >8% margin erosion. That keeps commercial flexibility and limits finance exposure.

I'll draft a short approval memo for Ben to include with the external proposal. We'll need VP sign-off if the expected discount (including onboarding credits) exceeds the 8% threshold; otherwise AM/Head can approve.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-24T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proforma commit adjustment request

Jane —

Thanks for the candid note and the proforma. We can accommodate a temporary reduction to your 12-month committed floor with a pragmatic guardrail. Proposed approach (concise):

1) Tiered start: 70% committed for Q1 and Q2, then ramp to 100% for the remainder of the 12-month term.
2) One-time onboarding credit: 4% credit applied across the first two invoices to offset operational disruption.
3) GPU-cost true-up: If our GPU cost index (public market blend) rises by more than 15% vs baseline, we will apply a pass-through up to a 20% cap on incremental cost. We'll include a short audit mechanism for the index (public exchange + agreed vendor feed).
4) Approval threshold: This package is pre-approved up to an expected margin impact of 8%. Any scenario with expected erosion >8% will require VP-level sign-off (finance).

Next steps: I attached a revised proforma (proforma_v2.xlsx) and redwood standard terms (redwood_terms_v3.pdf). If this looks acceptable, I'll send the DocuSign link for signature and loop legal for the indexation clause wording.

Proposed timeline: sign by 2027-06-03 to preserve the quoted pricing.

On copy: Karthik/Monica — please flag any implementation concerns (capacity scheduling, burst windows) before I send final to Novus. Lauren — I appreciate the memo; I'll escalate to VP only if the signed terms push beyond the 8% threshold.

Best,
Ben Carter
